project_type: Self-initiated personal product — cross-browser extension (Manifest V3), publicly published
project_description: A zero-dependency browser extension that injects a collapsible side panel into five AI chat platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok), listing every prompt the user has sent in the current conversation as a numbered, clickable outline with smooth scroll-to-prompt and hover previews. No backend, no database, no network requests, no analytics.

engineering_challenges.challenge: Five proprietary, obfuscated, frequently-changing SPA DOMs with no API and no shared markup convention
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Gemini renders prompts inside an Angular custom element; DeepSeek's only hook is a build-hashed class; Grok's is a generic Tailwind utility with high false-positive risk. No CI can test against any of them.
engineering_challenges.solution: Prioritised selector cascade with per-selector try/catch, per-platform text-extraction branches, and explicit fail-soft UI with a Refresh action

engineering_challenges.challenge: SPA conversation-change detection without router access
engineering_challenges.why_hard: A content script cannot hook a host SPA's router; Gemini sometimes changes only the URL hash on conversation switch
engineering_challenges.solution: Per-platform URL parsing including the hash, named sentinel fallbacks, and a document.body MutationObserver comparing location.href as a route-change proxy, with panel visibility captured before and restored after state reset

engineering_challenges.why_hard: Module-level state silently vanishes on teardown, and alert() does not exist in a worker/event-page context at all, so that feedback path was dead code
engineering_challenges.solution: chrome.storage.local for panel state, chrome.notifications.create() for off-platform feedback, async/await with try/catch

engineering_challenges.challenge: Style isolation inside five hostile host pages with their own theming
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Host global CSS and nested flex layouts broke the panel's scroll container intermittently and differently per platform
engineering_challenges.solution: Inline styles as primary mechanism, z-index 9999999, fixed positioning, a full font stack on every injected element, absolute-positioned scroll container with explicit top/bottom, and a post-open verification pass at 0/1000/2000ms

engineering_challenges.challenge: Packaging an over-privileged development build for public store review
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Ten web-accessible script files is a real attack surface and a predictable review flag; the scripting permission produces the scariest install warning
engineering_challenges.solution: Consolidated to one content script, dropped scripting, removed the legacy chat.openai.com origin, reduced web_accessible_resources to icons/*

decisions.decision: Split into ten modules (19 Mar 2025), then revert to a single content.js (by 5 Apr 2025)
decisions.reasoning: INFERRED: MV3 content scripts are not ES modules; ten plain scripts means ten globals, a manifest load-order contract, and ten web-accessible files
decisions.tradeoff: A 1,684-line file with no module boundaries — the project's main maintainability cost
decisions.evidence_level: Decision VERIFIED by manifest comparison; reasoning INFERRED

decisions.problem: Panel styling must survive uncontrolled host CSS
decisions.decision: Inline style assignment as the primary mechanism rather than a stylesheet
decisions.tradeoff: Styling scattered through logic, no theming layer, styles.css became partly vestigial
decisions.result: Consistent appearance across all five platforms
decisions.alternative_today: Shadow DOM, which gives isolation and a clean stylesheet

decisions.problem: The product's input is the user's own prompt text
decisions.decision: No backend, no telemetry, no analytics
decisions.reasoning: Trust posture for a high-sensitivity input; stated in the privacy policy and corroborated by the code
decisions.tradeoff: The product has no idea how it is used — no funnel, no retention data, no selector-breakage alerting
decisions.result: Verifiable privacy property; a dossier with thin metrics as the direct consequence

decisions.problem: Vendor DOM changes break selectors between releases
decisions.decision: Hard-code selectors in the shipped bundle rather than fetch a remote selector manifest
decisions.reasoning: INFERRED: a remote config would end the zero-network-request property
decisions.tradeoff: A vendor change can only be fixed by a new store release and review cycle
decisions.result: Privacy preserved; responsiveness to breakage sacrificed

decisions.decision: Self-injected fixed-position panel toggled by the toolbar action, not chrome.sidePanel
decisions.reasoning: chrome.sidePanel is Chromium-only and would fork the UI layer
decisions.tradeoff: Must fight host-page CSS rather than getting a native container

known_weaknesses: updateQuestionsList() looks up #questions-list, which createPanel() never creates (it creates #ai-prompts-navigator-questions) — the function returns early every time, making extractQuestions() and the observeChat() rendering pipeline vestigial. All live rendering happens through findChatQuestions().
observeUrlChanges() is defined twice (lines 537 and 1598) with identical bodies; the second silently wins
Chromium build still holds panelVisible in a module-level variable in an MV3 service worker — the bug diagnosed and fixed for Firefox was never back-ported
No automated tests of any kind, including for trivially testable pure functions (escapeHtml, URL parsing)
No version control for the extension code — history survives only as three dated zip archives and filesystem timestamps
Unmaintained since April 2025; at least the DeepSeek and Grok selectors are likely to have decayed, and current functional status is unverified
mouseout handler reads event.clientX/clientY from the implicit global rather than the handler parameter
lessons: Use version control even for a weekend project — the absence of git made this audit archaeology and is the single highest-value process change for future projects
Delete the old implementation when you write the new one — iterating by addition left half the message-extraction pipeline dead
Platform lifecycle beats platform API differences — the hardest part of the Firefox port was understanding that an MV3 background context is ephemeral, not chrome.* vs browser.*
Modularisation the platform fights is not worth it — but Shadow DOM plus a bundler would have given both isolation and structure

Privacy by construction has a cost and it should be a conscious one — collecting nothing means no visibility when a vendor DOM change silently breaks the product; an opt-in, local-only breakage signal is the middle ground
Shipping is a skill of its own — icons, privacy policy, landing page, store copy, permission justification and review were roughly as much elapsed work as the panel itself

high_confidence_quantified: Designed, built and published AI Prompts Navigator, a zero-dependency Manifest V3 browser extension that adds a clickable prompt outline to five AI chat platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok); live on all three major extension stores — Chrome, Edge and Firefox — with 64 store-reported users 18 months after release, rated 5.0 on Chrome, and running at zero infrastructure cost with no backend and no telemetry.

Took a solo product from idea to three approved public store listings in ~5 weeks, passing three independent third-party add-on reviews (Google, Microsoft, Mozilla) — including packaging, icon assets, privacy policy and permission justification for each.

Shipped a cross-browser extension from a single 1,684-line content script, byte-identical across Chromium and Gecko builds, with all platform divergence isolated to the manifest and background layer — including a diagnosed fix for MV3 background-context state loss using chrome.storage.local.
Cut the extension's requested privilege surface before release — removed one permission, one host origin and ten web-accessible script files — producing a minimum-privilege Chromium package.
high_confidence_non_quantified: Engineered a fail-soft DOM integration layer against five proprietary single-page applications with no public API and no stable markup contract, combining a prioritised five-tier selector cascade, per-platform text-extraction fallbacks, three independent retry ladders and an explicit recoverable empty state.

Solved SPA conversation-change detection without router access by parsing five distinct URL schemes (including Google Gemini's hash-only transitions) and using a MutationObserver on the document body as a route-change proxy, preserving UI state across navigation.

Built the product privacy-first by construction: zero network requests, zero analytics, zero third-party code, with all state confined to browser-local storage — a verifiable property of the shipped bundle rather than a policy promise.

Delivered an entire consumer product solo — UX, implementation, icon set, privacy policy, React/TypeScript marketing site with automated GitHub Pages deployment, store packaging and review response across three stores.
phrasing_warnings: Write '64 store-reported users across three stores', never '64 daily users' or '64 active users' — the three stores count differently and no cumulative install total is available.
Write 'rated 5.0 on Chrome (2 ratings)' or '4.67 average across 3 ratings', never a bare '5-star rated' — the sample is three.
Claim the permission narrowing, not that it shipped everywhere — the Edge listing carries the earlier permission set.

methodology.production_data_protocol: Not applicable. No .env, no credential, no connection string, no database and no backend exist in this project. No query of any kind was executed against any system. No credential, token or secret appears in any output file because none exists in the project.
methodology.store_metric_method: All three stores read on 2026-10-17, the same day, so the figures are contemporaneous even though their definitions differ. Firefox: AMO v5 API cross-checked against the rendered listing page, both agreeing. Edge: getproductdetailsbycrxid API returning activeInstallCount 24, ratingCount 0, and the package permission list. Chrome: public listing page reporting 21 users, 5.0 from 2 ratings, 86.73 KiB, last updated 2025-04-21 (the page does not expose a permission list). methodology.audit_history: During the original audit the Chrome and Edge listings could not be located by public search (exact product name, publisher name 'Clevali', and domain-restricted search against chromewebstore.google.com, chrome.google.com and microsoftedge.microsoft.com) and were recorded as UNKNOWN rather than assumed in either direction. The project owner supplied both URLs the same day and both were then measured directly. The original negative result is retained because 'the listing exists but is not discoverable by name search' is itself a fact worth knowing about the product's distribution.
methodology.attribution_method: Extension authorship attributed wholly to the project owner on the basis of the manifest author field, matching contact details across the AMO listing and git commits, the absence of any other contributor or vendored dependency, and the owner's own account. Landing-page authorship split explicitly by commit author, with the AI-generated portion named rather than absorbed.
